extracted.intended_audience: researchers and institutions preparing proposals for the FY25 MURI (DoD) funding opportunity (ONR/ARO/AFOSR)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory compliance requirements for organizations and investigators preparing white papers and full proposals for the FY25 MURI solicitation, including administrative certifications, reporting obligations, topic-specific research scope, and post-award reporting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Review Meeting hosting option
rubrics_metrics.description: "[Name of entity] offers the use of its facilities for a DoD Program Review Meeting to discuss the status of programs related to the subject of this proposal. Such meetings may include attendees representing multiple research efforts. The meetings will discuss only 'contracted fundamental research' ... No fee will be charged Program Review Meeting attendees. [Name of entity] understands it will not be asked to host a Performance Review Meeting more than once per year, if at all."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants interested in hosting should include an estimated cost and the foregoing language in their proposals; inclusion is optional and 'will not affect their selection for award.' If a contract is awarded, use of the facility will be included as an option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act (FFATA) compliance (2 CFR Part 170)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide information in their proposal that describes the necessary processes and systems in place to comply with the reporting requirements identified in 2 CFR Part 170 Appendix A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities are required to meet reporting requirements unless an exception or exemption applies. Refer to 2 CFR Part 170, including Appendix A, for detailed requirements, exceptions, and exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Assistance Certification (SF-424 (R&R) block 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Assistance Certifications Report is an attestation that the entity will abide by the requirements of the various laws and regulations and the supplemental at Section F.2.iv above. You are required to submit documentation, including the Standard Form-LLL 'Disclosure Form to Report Lobbying' (if applicable), and disclosure of any unpaid delinquent tax liability or a felony conviction under any Federal law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By checking 'I Agree' on SF-424 (R&R) block 17 applicants certify compliance with specified statutes; AFOSR-specific note: checking 'I Agree' certifies compliance with the Lobbying Disclosure Act and, if grant >$100,000, that you have no lobbying activity to disclose (if you do, attach SF-LLL). Instructions link provided for SF-LLL completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpaid Delinquent Federal Tax Liability / Felony Conviction representation
rubrics_metrics.description: By checking 'I Agree' on SF-424 (R&R) block 17 you represent that you are not a corporation that has any unpaid Federal tax liability that has been assessed ... and that you are not a corporation that was convicted of a felony criminal violation under any Federal law within the preceding 24 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot make this representation you are ineligible unless a Federal agency SDO has considered suspension or debarment and determined further action is not required. Applicants should provide information to the agency's SDO as soon as possible to facilitate consideration before award decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications Regarding Restrictions on Lobbying (31 U.S.C. 1352)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) No Federal appropriated funds have been paid or will be paid ... for influencing or attempting to influence an officer or employee of an agency, a Member of Congress ... (2) If funds other than Federal appropriated funds have been paid or will be paid ... the Applicant shall complete and submit Standard Form-LLL ... (3) The Applicant shall require that the language of this certification be included in the award documents for all subawards at all tiers ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of this certification is a prerequisite imposed by 31 U.S.C. 1352. Failure to file the required certification may subject the filer to civil penalties of not less than $10,000 and not more than $100,000 for each failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Using Funds with Entities that Require Certain Internal Confidentiality Agreements (GIC 19-02)
rubrics_metrics.description: By submission of its proposal or application, the Applicant represents that it does not require any of its employees, contractors, or subrecipients seeking to report fraud, waste, or abuse to sign or comply with internal confidentiality agreements or statements prohibiting or otherwise restricting those employees, contractors, or subrecipients from lawfully reporting that waste, fraud, or abuse to a designated investigative or law enforcement representative of a Federal department or agency authorized to receive such information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a certification supplement to SF-424 (R&R) block 17; signing the application certifies the statement and acknowledges potential penalties for false statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification Regarding Disclosure of Funding Sources (Section 223(a) NDAA FY2021)
rubrics_metrics.description: By checking 'I Agree' on SF-424 (R&R) block 17 you certify that (a) the PI and other key personnel certify that the current and pending support provided on the proposal is current, accurate and complete; (b) agree to update such disclosure at the request of the agency prior to the award of support and at any subsequent time the agency determines appropriate during the term of the award; and (c) the PI and other key personnel have been made aware of the requirements under Section 223(a)(1) of this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False statements may subject the signer to criminal, civil, or administrative penalties (U.S. code, Title 18, Section 1001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of Interest disclosure (2 CFR 200.318(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for assistance are required to comply with 2 CFR 200.318(c), Codes of Conduct, to prevent real or apparent conflicts of interest in the award and administration of any contracts by which a recipient or subrecipient purchases property or services, supported by federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You and your organization must disclose any potential or actual scientific or nonscientific conflict(s) of interest to the agency, and for any identified subrecipient included in your application. The agency may request additional information or a conflict of interest mitigation plan, subject to agency approval. Disclose all collaborators in the list of current and pending support even if they did not formally provide support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Conduct requirement (2 CFR 200.318(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for assistance are required to comply with 2 CFR 200.318(c), Codes of Conduct, to prevent real or apparent conflicts of interest in the award and administration of any contracts supported by federal funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision will be incorporated into all assistance instruments awarded under this FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review participation and confidentiality requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of proposals funded as basic research, DoD may utilize peer reviewers from academia, industry, and Government agencies to assist in the periodic appraisal of performance under the awards. Peer reviewers who are not U.S. Government employees must sign nondisclosure agreements before receiving full or partial copies of proposals and reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviews monitor the quality of funded research and help determine continued funding. Applicants may include travel costs for the PI to attend peer review. Peer reviews may consider information from individual project or program review meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on procurement of foreign-made COTS Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial Off The Shelf Unmanned Aircraft Systems (COTS UAS) may not be purchased pursuant to this grant or contract or other transaction agreement for prototype until a waiver per the Deputy Secretary of Defense Memorandum 'Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities,' May 23, 2018 is obtained by the cognizant DoD Program Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: a waiver is not required when research is supported via a grant award AND it is unclassified and funded with either basic research funds (6.1) or applied research funds (6.2) and performed on campus by a university. Waivers are required for other grants/assistance agreements except the stated campus/basic-research exception, and are required for all contract awards and other transaction agreements. Waiver always required for efforts involving military personnel, DoD property/facilities, US Government labs, UARCs, FFRDCs, PAO, classified work, or work exploring specific military utility. Prospective performers must notify the cognizant DoD Program Officer of anticipated COTS UAS purchases at white paper/proposal time or upon award changes and provide documentation; performers must cooperate to support waiver and Cyber Vulnerability Assessment. No federal funds shall be expended for such purchases until waiver and assessments are complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Recipient Integrity and Performance Matters (2 CFR Part 200 Appendix XII)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Federal share of any Federal award includes more than $500,000 over the period of performance, the post award reporting requirements, Award Term and Condition for Recipient Integrity and Performance Matters (2 CFR Part 200 Appendix XII), are applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the subsequent subclauses for details on who must report and what must be reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to maintain and report integrity/performance information (SAM/FAPIIS) for large recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: If the total value of your currently active grants, cooperative agreements, and procurement contracts from all Federal awarding agencies exceeds $10,000,000 ... then you as the recipient ... must maintain the currency of information reported to the System for Award Management (SAM) that is made available in the designated integrity and performance system (currently FAPIIS) about civil, criminal, or administrative proceedings described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information posted in the designated integrity and performance system on or after April 15, 2011 (except past performance reviews required for procurement contracts) will be publicly available. This is a statutory requirement under 41 U.S.C. 2313.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings required to be reported under recipient integrity rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit information about each proceeding that: (a) is in connection with the award or performance of a Federal award; (b) reached final disposition during the most recent five-year period; and (c) is one of: (1) a criminal proceeding that resulted in a conviction; (2) a civil proceeding that resulted in a finding of fault and payment of a monetary fine, penalty, reimbursement, restitution, or damages of $5,000 or more; (3) an administrative proceeding that resulted in a finding of fault and your payment of either a monetary fine or penalty of $5,000 or more or reimbursement, restitution, or damages in excess of $100,000; or (4) any other proceeding that could have led to those outcomes or had a disposition by consent or compromise with acknowledgement of fault.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not report audits, site visits, corrective plans, or deliverable inspections. Ensure disclosures do not conflict with applicable laws and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting procedures, frequency, and lookback period for integrity matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter in the SAM Entity Management area the information that SAM requires about each proceeding described. You must report proceedings information through SAM for the most recent five-year period, either to report new information or affirm no new information to report. Recipients with cumulative Federal awards greater than $10,000,000 must disclose semiannually any information about the criminal, civil, and administrative proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You do not need to submit information again via assistance awards if already provided through SAM under Federal procurement contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relevant to recipient integrity reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative proceeding means a non-judicial process adjudicatory in nature to make a determination of fault or liability (examples given). Conviction means a judgment or conviction of a criminal offense by any court of competent jurisdiction, including nolo contendere. Total value of currently active awards includes only the Federal share and includes expected funding increments and options even if not yet exercised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions clarify scope and thresholds for reporting obligations under Appendix XII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award reporting formats and agency-specific instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: For ONR: post award reporting requirements are under the ONR Addendum to the DoD R&D General Terms and Conditions and ONR Programmatic Requirements (link provided). For ARO: see ARO Form 18 'Reporting Instructions' for submission and formatting. For AFOSR: use the Federal-wide Research Progress Performance Report (RPPR) for interim, annual, and final reports and submit interim/final reports to specified AFOSR community site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Federal-wide RPPR format is under development; performers do not have to use the RPPR now but DoD plans to use it in the future and may issue an award modification requiring use after Federal Register notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications and question submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All UNCLASSIFIED communications shall be submitted via e-mail to the Technical Point of Contact with a copy to the designated Business POC. Questions should be concise, reference the relevant FOA part and paragraph. Questions submitted within 2 weeks prior to a submission deadline may not be answered, and the due date will not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the FedConnect message center to submit white paper responses or questions related to this announcement; email the appropriate point of contact listed in Section G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 1 (Superatom-based materials) — Objective and Research Concentration Areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective: identify the interactions that control the novel transport properties in superatom-based materials, and develop the understanding needed to design, synthesize, and characterize these materials to exploit their novel energy transport properties. Research Concentration Areas: (1) Characterization of novel properties, especially electronic and spin transport, to identify underlying coherent transport mechanism; (2) Theoretical/computational methods/design rules to predict and optimize transport properties and guide synthetic routes; (3) Synthesis of novel materials based on nanoscale building blocks such as superatoms or molecular clusters; (4) Exploration of other novel properties and possible uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipated resources: awards under this topic will be no more than $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting no more than 7 funded faculty researchers; exceptions should be discussed with the topic chief during the white paper phase. Research Topic Chiefs and references are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 2 (Moiré-engineered oxide bicrystals) — Objective and Research Concentration Areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Objectives: elucidate the fundamental structures and physics, locally and over distance, of bicrystalline oxides formed by Moiré engineering. Research Concentration Areas: (1) processing studies to produce suitable membranes including control of composition, thickness, and surface termination; (2) nanoscale structural and chemical studies (electron microscopy, local spectroscopy, synchrotron techniques); (3) mapping of strain fields; (4) first-principles modeling of nanoscale structure and local properties; (5) mesoscale modeling relating periodic structures to selected electronic, magnetic, and optoelectronic properties requiring atomic-to-continuum and multiscale methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipated resources: investment of $1.5M per year for five years, supporting up to seven funded faculty researchers. Research Topic Chiefs and references are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic 3 (Energy and information processing in biological organisms) — Objective and Research Concentration Areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective: support investigations of relationships between energy consumption and information processing in biological organisms to identify strategies with implications for human and computer performance in energy-constrained environments. Research Concentration Areas may include: (1) information processing strategies that trade reduced energy consumption with graceful degradations in computation; (2) factors impacting the metabolic/energetic cost of an information bit; (3) predictions from biophysically-realistic models of information processing; (4) implications for human perceptual and cognitive performance under caloric restrictions; (5) information theory-based computational strategies for artificial systems in energy-constrained conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers should specify their definition of 'information' and associated measure(s) appropriate for their research questions. Anticipated resources: awards no larger than $1.5M per year for five years and fund no more than six faculty researchers; exceptions should be discussed with topic chiefs during white paper phase. Research Topic Chiefs and references are provided.
